recovery.limits: All four complete-class trials passed with existing skips, and no accumulator-serialization warnings were observed. Near-capacity GC heap samples establish pressure, not the cause of the original missing-accumulator failure. These instrumented trials are not a controlled speedup comparison.

initial_attempt.observed: Diagnostic setup could not load the newly added timing helper from a stale standalone dependency. No Fluss test execution attribution was obtained. The replacement uses the current complete Maven reactor.

jfr.limits: Java execution samples and native-method stack samples are separate. Native samples include blocking I/O and are not CPU attribution. Inclusive counts overlap. Neither sample count is exact CPU time. Native samples do not resolve Rust internals. Compilation durations are activity intervals, not compiler CPU seconds. Allocation weights are sampled estimates. Wait durations exclude unrecorded short waits, overlap across threads and are not CPU time. GC activity is not total stop-the-world pause time; heap summaries are maxima at recorded GC boundaries, not peak RSS. Instrumented elapsed times are not speedup evidence.

fluss.limits: Elapsed and child CPU include the complete current Maven reactor; child CPU excludes external broker containers. The 29-case instrumented pass is attribution, not speedup evidence. Every test closes two independent catalogs sequentially in the baseline.

recovery_transport.method: Two alternating pairs, fresh JVMs, fixed 2 GiB heap, first-tier compilation, ordinary NOP logging, no JFR or phase timers. All original class assertions and individual outcomes retained. Encoded-size and point-in-time heap messages retained in both modes.
